blogs.title: The Second-Trimester CA-125 Trap: Why Elevated Markers Don't Always Mean Malignancy
blogs.description: This post explores the physiological fluctuations of tumor markers during pregnancy, specifically focusing on CA-125. We will analyze why the 'normal' reference range shifts across trimesters, discuss the pitfalls of relying on isolated marker elevations in a 40-year-old multipara, and review the case where a CA-125 of 41.8 U/mL led to unnecessary anxiety despite being a benign finding.

blogs.title: Pediatric vs. Obstetric Dilemma: When to Operate on Symptomatic Leiomyomas in Pregnancy
blogs.description: Focusing on the tension between expectant management and surgical intervention, this article dissects the indications for myomectomy during pregnancy. Using the case's progression from pain and dyspnea to confirmed torsion/necrosis, we will establish a risk-benefit framework for deciding when to operate versus waiting for delivery, highlighting the specific triggers (torsion, infection, obstruction) that mandate immediate action.

blogs.title: The Art of Selective Resection: Leaving Masses Behind to Save a Fetus
blogs.description: Not all masses need removal to ensure a healthy outcome. This post analyzes the surgical strategy employed in this case: removing the symptomatic, pedunculated upper mass while leaving the deep pelvic mass intact. We will discuss the rationale behind selective resection to minimize uterine trauma, reduce bleeding risk, and prevent preterm labor, illustrating how 'doing less' can sometimes be the most effective obstetric maneuver.

blogs.title: Imaging Without Gadolinium: Decoding Complex Abdominal Masses in Pregnant Patients
blogs.description: With CT contraindicated and ultrasound limited by body habitus and gestational size, MRI becomes the gold standard. This educational piece reviews the safety profile of non-contrast MRI in pregnancy (avoiding gadolinium), interprets specific signal characteristics (T1/T2 fat-sat findings) seen in this case that distinguished cystic degeneration from malignancy, and provides a practical algorithm for radiologic workup of abdominal masses in G1P0 women >35 years old.
